summary: Germany records nationality, never ethnicity. Police statistics publish child victims and suspects by nationality for child sexual abuse and child maltreatment, plus official suspect rates for Germans and non-Germans; courts publish German vs foreign convictions; child-protection statistics record whether a child's parent comes from abroad. Because 'German' includes naturalised and dual citizens, these are proxies, and no source can identify European descent.

nations.Federal (BKA, Destatis): Police statistics (PKS) and court statistics by nationality, child-protection statistics by parental origin. One nationality per person; German takes precedence.
nations.North Rhine-Westphalia: Since 1 July 2025 police record all citizenships of suspects and victims; 17.5% of German suspects in 2025 held another citizenship. Not yet published for child offences.
nations.Bavaria: Annual PKS report gives German, non-German and Zuwanderer shares (e.g. sexual offences: 32.0% non-German suspects); no child-specific nationality table found in the report.
nations.Berlin: Annual PKS short report gives case counts for child sexual abuse (1,013) and child maltreatment (385) and nationality for all suspects (47.3% non-German); no child-specific nationality table found.

groups.label: Zuwanderer (asylum seekers, refugees, tolerated, unlawful stay)

european_note: German data record citizenship (and, in child protection and surveys, migration background), never ethnicity or descent. 'German' covers native Germans, naturalised citizens and dual nationals alike, and 'non-German' mixes EU, other European and non-European citizens. So European descent cannot be identified for victims or perpetrators. The EU and Other European nationality groups are the closest proxy and cover only foreign citizens.
european_title: Not recorded by any German source

harms.label: Child endangerment cases (child protection, §8a)
harms.intro: Youth welfare offices completed 268,294 child-endangerment assessments in 2025 and confirmed 79,792 cases of acute or latent endangerment. Neglect was involved in 57.8%, psychological abuse in 37.6%, physical abuse in 29.1% and sexual violence in 5.4% (more than one type possible). A parent was the main source of the endangerment in 74.3% of cases.

victims.scope: Germany, confirmed acute or latent endangerment, 2025
victims.rate_label: children with confirmed endangerment per 100,000 children of the same group
victims.rate_note: Calculated here: Destatis counts divided by Mikrozensus 2025 first-results estimates of under-18s with and without a migration background (under-15 bands plus 3/5 of the 15-19 band). The two definitions are close but not identical (§8a asks whether a parent comes from abroad; the Mikrozensus asks whether the person or a parent was born without German citizenship), so rates are approximate.
victims.share_note: The variable is whether at least one parent comes from abroad ('ausländische Herkunft'), regardless of the parents' current citizenship. That is a migration-background proxy, not ethnicity, and it cannot separate European from non-European origin. Destatis's headline 33.5% counts only children whose family also mainly speaks a language other than German.

perpetrators.text: The §8a statistics record the person causing the endangerment only by relationship (mother, father, other relative, etc.), not by nationality or origin.

cross.text: No perpetrator origin is recorded, so no victim-by-perpetrator table is possible.

harms.label: Physical abuse (police: Misshandlung von Kindern)
harms.intro: Police recorded 4,630 child victims under 14 of 'Misshandlung von Kindern' (§225 StGB, abuse of children in one's care) in 2025, and 3,784 suspects. Nationality is recorded for both; ethnicity is not.

victims.share_note: Nationality, not ethnicity. 'German' includes naturalised and dual citizens (the PKS counts anyone holding German citizenship as German). Non-German includes stateless people. Sub-groups: EU = other 26 EU states; Other Europe excludes the EU and Türkei.
victims.rate_label: child victims per 100,000 children under 14 of the same nationality group
victims.rate_note: Calculated here: PKS victims divided by Destatis population under 14 at 31 Dec 2024 (Census-2022 base). Victims of unknown nationality (1.7%) are left out of both group rates.

perpetrators.share_note: Nationality, not ethnicity. 'German' includes naturalised and dual citizens (the PKS counts anyone holding German citizenship as German). Non-German includes stateless people. Sub-groups: EU = other 26 EU states; Other Europe excludes the EU and Türkei. Zuwanderer = asylum seekers, people with protection status, tolerated people and people staying unlawfully (a sub-set of non-Germans across many nationalities).
perpetrators.rate_label: suspects per 100,000 residents aged 8+ of the same nationality group (BKA Tatverdächtigenbelastungszahl)
perpetrators.rate_note: Official BKA rates (PKS 2025, Census-2022-based population at 31 Dec 2024). Only suspects living in Germany are counted, so tourists and people without a registered address are excluded. Not adjusted for age or sex: non-German residents are on average younger and more often male, which raises their crude rate.

cross.text: The PKS records victim and suspect nationality in the same case, but no table links them for child victims. The BKA's migration report links German and 'Zuwanderer' victims and suspects for all ages and broad offence groups only.

data.scope: Germany, people convicted with §225 as principal offence, 2024
data.rate_reason: Counts too small for rates. Destatis groups stateless and unknown nationality with foreigners.
data.share_note: Destatis Strafverfolgung 2024: 64 German, 22 foreign. §225 covers abuse of any dependant, not only children.

harms.label: Sexual abuse of children (police and courts)
harms.intro: Police recorded 17,126 cases of child sexual abuse (§§176-176e StGB) in 2025, with 18,736 victims under 14 and 12,823 suspects. In 54% of cases victim and suspect knew each other. Courts convicted 1,855 people under §§176-176e in 2024.

victims.share_note: Nationality, not ethnicity. 'German' includes naturalised and dual citizens (the PKS counts anyone holding German citizenship as German). Non-German includes stateless people. Sub-groups: EU = other 26 EU states; Other Europe excludes the EU and Türkei. Victims of §176 offences are under 14 by definition.
victims.rate_label: child victims per 100,000 children under 14 of the same nationality group
victims.rate_note: Calculated here: PKS victims divided by Destatis population under 14 at 31 Dec 2024. 1,771 victims (9.5%) have unknown or unclear nationality and are left out of both group rates, so the non-German rate in particular may be understated.

perpetrators.share_note: Nationality, not ethnicity. 'German' includes naturalised and dual citizens (the PKS counts anyone holding German citizenship as German). Non-German includes stateless people. Sub-groups: EU = other 26 EU states; Other Europe excludes the EU and Türkei. Zuwanderer = asylum seekers, people with protection status, tolerated people and people staying unlawfully.
perpetrators.rate_label: suspects per 100,000 residents aged 8+ of the same nationality group (BKA Tatverdächtigenbelastungszahl)
perpetrators.rate_note: Official BKA rates (PKS 2025, Census-2022-based population at 31 Dec 2024). Only suspects living in Germany are counted, so tourists and people without a registered address are excluded. Not adjusted for age or sex: non-German residents are on average younger and more often male, which raises their crude rate. 31.4% of suspects were under 18.

cross.text: No table links child victims' nationality to suspects' nationality. The BKA's migration report gives, for all ages and all sexual offences in 2025: 2,941 German victims of offences with at least one Zuwanderer suspect, 650 Zuwanderer victims of Zuwanderer suspects, and 160 Zuwanderer victims of German suspects. It has no reverse figure for German victims of German suspects and is not child-specific.

data.rate_reason: Destatis publishes convictions by German/foreign only at this offence detail; nationality detail exists only for broad offence groups.
data.share_note: 1,545 German, 310 foreign (Destatis counts stateless and unknown with foreigners). Calculated here from Destatis table 24311-47.

harms.label: Parental violence (survey, Lower Saxony)
harms.intro: The Niedersachsensurvey 2024 asked ninth-graders in Lower Saxony about violence from their parents. 32.3% reported physical parental violence before age 12. Germany has no national survey of child abuse by origin; the 2025 Ulm national study (12.7% of adults reported childhood sexual violence) publishes no breakdown by migration background.

victims.rate_note: KFN Forschungsbericht 171. Migration generation is self-reported. Last 12 months: 21.3% (first generation), 22.3% (second), 12.6% (no migration history). One state only; non-government academic source funded by the state.
victims.share_note: Migration background, not ethnicity or nationality.

perpetrators.text: The perpetrators are the pupils' parents; their origin is inferred from the pupil's migration generation, not recorded separately.

Nationality of child victims is not published separately, so the figures below cover all ages.

harms.intro: Police recorded 41,677 cases of distributing, acquiring, possessing or producing child sexual abuse material in 2025, with 34,819 suspects. Courts convicted 4,562 people under §184b in 2024 (84.8% German).

harms.label: Commercial sexual exploitation of minors
harms.intro: The BKA's trafficking report counted 164 minor victims of commercial sexual exploitation in 132 concluded investigations in 2025 (232 in 2024), 82% aged 14-17 and 75% female, and 181 suspects. 60 victims were first contacted online.

victims.rate_reason: Counts too small for reliable rates.
victims.share_note: 119 German. Most common non-German nationalities: Romanian (7), then Bulgarian, Filipino, Serbian and Syrian (3 each). The report does not say whether any victim's nationality was unknown, so the non-German share may include unknowns. Nationality only.

§8a neglect cases by parental origin (yes/no). Perpetrators only via the narrow §171 police offence by nationality.

components.name: Victim heritage
components.full: Official data by harm that separately identify children of European descent (e.g. White non-Hispanic, White British) alongside every other group, self-reported or official, few unknowns. Broad categories that lump European-descent people with others get partial credit; proxies (nationality, citizenship, migration background, country of birth) at most 9.4 points.

components.name: Perpetrator heritage
components.full: Same standard for perpetrators: not perceived, few unknowns, European descent separately identified. Proxies at most 9.4 points.

components.name: Coverage and missing data
components.full: Over 90% of the population covered, under 10% unknown

components.name: Rates and linkage
components.full: Rates per 100,000 possible, and victim heritage linked to perpetrator heritage

score.gold_standard: 100% means a country publishes data that separately identifies people of European descent, both as perpetrators (so one can tell when they disproportionately harm a group) and as child victims (so one can tell when European-descent children are disproportionately harmed), alongside every other group, linked victim to perpetrator, for every harm.
score.rules: Heritage is 75 of every 100 points (victims 37.5, perpetrators 37.5); coverage, rates and access share the other 25. Proxies such as nationality or migration background earn at most a quarter of the heritage points. A country with no real ethnicity data for victims or perpetrators is capped at 25%.
score.why: Germany scores 25% on the stricter scale (20-40%), down from 49%. It records nationality and migration background but never ethnicity, so every heritage point is a proxy capped at a quarter of the heritage marks. Its good coverage, open access and official rates lift its uncapped total to 29%, but a country with no real ethnicity data on either side is capped at 25%.
score.proxy_note: Every German figure is a proxy (nationality or migration background), so heritage earns at most a quarter of its points, and a country with no real ethnicity data is capped at 25%. Germany's uncapped total is about 29%, from its coverage, open access and official rates. On the old scale it scored 49%.
score.weights_id: harm weights of 19 Nov 2026 (homicide 25, sexual abuse 20, sex trafficking 20, physical abuse 15, online exploitation 10, neglect 10)

pks_age.name: Polizeiliche Kriminalstatistik 2025: victims by age and sex (table 91)
pks_age.records: Victims of each offence key by age band (under 6, 6-13, 14-17, 18-20, 21-59, 60+) and sex, completed and attempted. Key 892500 (murder, manslaughter and killing on request), completed: 47 victims under 6, 37 aged 6-13, 35 aged 14-17.
pks_age.limitations: No nationality in this table; the nationality table (911) has no age.

pks_victims.name: Polizeiliche Kriminalstatistik 2025: victims by nationality (table 911)
pks_victims.records: Victims of each offence key by single nationality (about 190 codes), completed and attempted, all ages.
pks_victims.limitations: Nationality only, no ethnicity or migration background; German includes dual and naturalised citizens. Child age not crossed with nationality, so child victims are identifiable only for child-specific offences (§176, Misshandlung von Kindern). Police-recorded crime only.

pks_suspects.name: Polizeiliche Kriminalstatistik 2025: suspects by nationality (table 62), Zuwanderer (table 56) and suspect rates (tables 20, 40, 50)
pks_suspects.records: Suspects by offence key and single nationality; Zuwanderer suspects by age and sex; official suspect rates per 100,000 for Germans and non-Germans.
pks_suspects.limitations: 'Personen, die sowohl die deutsche als auch eine andere Staatsangehörigkeit besitzen, werden als Deutsche gezählt.' Suspects, not convicted offenders. Rates are crude (not age-standardised) and cover residents only.

blb_sex.name: Bundeslagebild Sexualdelikte zum Nachteil von Kindern und Jugendlichen 2025
blb_sex.years: Annual since 2023 (replacing the joint BKA-UBSKM "Kindliche Gewaltopfer" release); 2025 edition 21 Jul 2026
blb_sex.records: Child and youth sexual abuse, abuse material, exploitation, with victim and suspect profiles.
blb_sex.limitations: Built on the PKS; nationality only. Its 18.2% non-German share of child victims includes 1,746 children of unclear nationality.

bka_mh.name: Bundeslagebild Menschenhandel und Ausbeutung 2025
bka_mh.records: Concluded trafficking and exploitation investigations, including commercial sexual exploitation of minors, with victim and suspect nationality.
bka_mh.limitations: Small counts; concluded investigations only; nationality only, mostly top nationalities in text.

zuwanderung.name: Bundeslagebild Kriminalität im Kontext von Zuwanderung 2025
zuwanderung.records: Crime by and against Zuwanderer, including suspect-victim constellations (Zuwanderer vs German) for all offences, sexual offences and homicide.
zuwanderung.limitations: All ages; Zuwanderer are a legal-status group, not an ethnicity; German-on-German constellation not given; not child-specific (8.6% of Zuwanderer victims were children).

destatis_sv.name: Strafverfolgungsstatistik 2024 (Statistischer Bericht)
destatis_sv.years: Annual; 2024 data published 21 Nov 2025; 2025 edition not yet out
destatis_sv.records: Convictions by detailed offence and German/foreign; foreign convictions by continent and nationality for broad offence groups; offences against child victims (no nationality).
destatis_sv.limitations: German vs foreign only at paragraph level (§176, §184b, §225); stateless and unknown counted as foreign; no victim data except a count of child-victim offences.

destatis_8a.name: Statistik der Gefährdungseinschätzungen nach §8a SGB VIII, 2025
destatis_8a.records: Child-endangerment assessments by outcome, type of endangerment, age, sex, foreign origin of a parent, family language, and relationship of the person causing it.
destatis_8a.limitations: Origin of the child's parents only (from abroad or not), no nationality detail or ethnicity; nothing on the person who caused the harm besides relationship.

hze_def.name: Child and youth welfare statistics: variable definition (ausländische Herkunft)
hze_def.records: Defines the origin item: whether the mother and/or father come from abroad; 'the parents' current citizenship is not decisive'.
hze_def.limitations: Verified on the HzE (support) form guidance; assumed to be the same item in the §8a statistics, which use the same wording. Not confirmed on a §8a-specific form.

mikrozensus.name: Mikrozensus 2025 first results: population by migration background and age
mikrozensus.records: Population with and without migration background by age band (thousands); also the newer Einwanderungsgeschichte concept.
mikrozensus.limitations: Survey estimates; age bands do not split at 18, so under-18 figures are approximated here.

population.name: Bevölkerungsfortschreibung (Census 2022 base), 31 Dec 2024
population.records: Population by age, sex and German/non-German citizenship.

destatis_dc.name: Todesursachenstatistik (cause of death): assault deaths by age
destatis_dc.records: Deaths from assault (X85-Y09) by age and sex.
destatis_dc.limitations: No nationality or migration background with cause of death.

nrw.name: NRW: recording of multiple citizenships in the police statistics
nrw.publisher: Ministerium des Innern NRW; Landtag NRW
nrw.years: Since 1 Jul 2025; first full year in PKS NRW 2025
nrw.records: NRW police now record every citizenship of suspects and victims; 51,960 German suspects (17.5%) held at least one other citizenship in 2025.
nrw.limitations: NRW only; the BKA still receives one nationality; no dual-citizenship breakdown for child offences was found (only for knife crime).

kfn.name: Niedersachsensurvey 2024 (KFN Forschungsbericht 171)
kfn.years: Repeated school survey; 2024 wave published Oct 2025
kfn.records: Ninth-graders' self-reported victimisation, including parental violence, by migration generation.
kfn.limitations: Non-government academic source. One state; migration background, not ethnicity.

ulm.name: National prevalence study of sexual violence in childhood (Universitätsklinikum Ulm, Deutsches Ärzteblatt 2025)
ulm.records: 12.7% of adults reported childhood or adolescent sexual violence (20.6% of women, 4.8% of men).
ulm.limitations: Non-government academic source. No breakdown by migration background published.

proxy_note: Germany records nationality (citizenship) or migration background, never ethnicity. Every group below is a proxy, not ethnicity.
availability_note: Each harm has an 'availability' map listing the victim and perpetrator groups with any published figure (overall and by measure) and any linked victim-perpetrator pairs. Groups not listed have no data for that harm; the explorer should grey them out rather than offer an empty combination.
